name: Armenia: Yerevan, Dilijan and the south

cities.base: Kentron, in the blocks between Republic Square, Saryan Street and the foot of the Cascade. Everything you will do on foot is inside that fifteen minute triangle, the wine bars and the late food are on
cities.name: Yerevan

cities.base: Nobody sleeps out here and nobody needs to. Garni is 32km east of Yerevan and Geghard another 9km up the valley, so it is a half day from a Kentron hotel; the one reason to stay in Garni village is th
cities.name: Garni, Geghard and the Azat gorge

cities.base: Sevan town is a Soviet leftover and the west shore hotels are grim, so treat the lake as the stop on the drive between Yerevan and Dilijan rather than a bed. If you insist on a night, sleep at Tsapata
cities.name: Lake Sevan

cities.base: The old town end around Sharambeyan Street, not the highway strip. You can walk to dinner, the Transcaucasian Trail head for Jukhtak is fifteen minutes west, and the Haghartsin and Gosh valleys are bo
cities.name: Dilijan

cities.base: A guesthouse in Areni village itself or in Yeghegnadzor 20km east. Sleeping here is what lets you actually drink at three cellars instead of sipping and driving on, and it breaks the four hour Yerevan
cities.name: Areni and the Vayots Dzor wine road

cities.base: The stone grid in the centre, within walking distance of the market and the river. Goris is the only town in Syunik with real beds and real dinner, and it puts you 40 minutes from the Halidzor cable c
cities.name: Goris

cities.base: There are two or three guesthouses in Tatev village and they are fine, but the monastery is a day out of Goris and the cable car does not run early enough to reward sleeping up there. Ride from Halidz
cities.name: Tatev

places.name: Republic Square and the fountains
places.note: Tamanyan's oval of pink and black tufa, finished under Stalin and still the best built thing in the country; the musical fountains run on summer evenings from about 21:00 and stop for the winter.

places.name: History Museum of Armenia
places.note: Bronze Age carts, Urartian bronzes and the Areni shoe in one building; the Urartu floor is the reason to go and the labelling in English thins out badly on the upper floors.

places.name: Matenadaran
places.note: Seventeen thousand manuscripts in a tufa bunker above the avenue, of which maybe seventy are on show; pay for the guide or you are looking at beautiful books you cannot read.

places.name: The Cascade and the Cafesjian sculpture garden
places.note: Botero's fat cat and a Lynn Chadwick sit on the terraces for free and the escalators inside save your legs; the Cafesjian galleries inside the steps open Friday to Sunday only, and Ararat shows from the top just after dawn before the haze.

places.name: Armenian Genocide Museum-Institute at Tsitsernakaberd
places.note: Free, underground, and the single thing that explains why the rest of the country looks the way it does; go before lunch and do not schedule anything cheerful for the two hours after.

places.name: Sergei Parajanov Museum
places.note: Collages the film director made from buttons, lace and broken dolls while he was in and out of Soviet prison; the smallest museum in Yerevan and the one people remember.

places.name: GUM Market
places.note: Dried fruit, sujukh ropes, barrels of pickles and forty sellers who will all feed you slices of the same apricot; the cheese and basturma counters at the back are where the actual shopping happens.

places.name: Vernissage
places.note: Full size Saturday and Sunday, half empty midweek; carpets, Soviet cameras, duduks and a lot of identical obsidian. Bargain and check that a carpet is not machine made.

places.name: ARARAT brandy factory tour
places.note: The standard tour walks the aging cellar and pours the three star and the seven year Ani; book ahead, and pay the extra for the ten and twenty year pour if brandy is the point rather than the photo.

places.name: Lavash
places.note: Glass walled tonir, good ghapama and dolma, and an Armenian wine list that is actually chosen rather than assembled; heavily booked and worth the two days notice.

places.name: In Vino on Saryan Street
places.note: Saryan is now a solid block of wine bars and this is the one that started it; ask for Voskehat and Areni from small producers rather than the supermarket labels, sit outside, and finish at the Tumanyan Street shaurma counters, which run past midnight.

places.name: Echmiadzin Cathedral and the Treasury
places.note: Seat of the Armenian Church since 301 and arguably the oldest cathedral anywhere, 20km west of the city on the airport road; the long restoration has left the interior plainer than the photographs suggest, so budget time for the Treasury museum instead.

places.name: Garni Temple
places.note: First century Ionic temple on a spur above the Azat gorge, blown down by the 1679 earthquake and put back up between 1969 and 1976, so most of what you touch is Soviet reassembly of original stone.

places.name: The Roman bathhouse mosaic at Garni
places.note: Inside the same ticket, under a shed twenty metres from the temple: a Greek sea-god floor whose inscription translates as we worked and got nothing. Most groups walk straight past it.

places.name: The Symphony of Stones
places.note: Hexagonal basalt columns hanging over the riverbed below Garni, free, reached by a rough 2km road that a normal hire car will manage slowly; go before the tour vans at 11:00.

places.name: Geghard Monastery
places.note: Half of it is cut into the cliff rather than built, and the acoustics in the rock-hewn Avazan chamber are the reason to be there when a chant group turns up; free, and busy from mid morning.

places.name: The gata and sweet sujukh stalls at Geghard
places.note: Women sell gata straight off a tray and walnut strings dipped in grape must; the sujukh keeps for weeks and travels better than anything you will buy at Vernissage.

places.name: Havuts Tar
places.note: Ten kilometres there and back from Garni across the river and up the far side to a ruined eleventh century monastery nobody maintains; no shade, no water, and the best view of the gorge in the country.

places.name: Baking lavash in a Garni tonir
places.note: A village house lets you slap dough onto the wall of a clay pit oven and then feeds you what comes out with cheese and herbs; arrange through your driver or guesthouse the day before.

places.name: Khorovats lunch in Garni village
places.note: Pork ribs and whole aubergines over vine cuttings, with tan and the house tuti oghi; every second house on the main road does it and the difference between them is small.

places.name: The Charents Arch
places.note: A 1957 stone arch on the Garni road framing Ararat, with the poet's lines cut into it; five minutes, worth the stop only on a clear morning before the plain hazes over.

places.name: Aghjots Vank
places.note: A thirteenth century ruin an hour and a half up a rough track from the Garni side, with carved reliefs still in place because almost nobody goes; needs a 4x4 or a real walk.

places.name: Sevanavank
places.note: Two ninth century churches on what was an island until the Soviets dropped the lake twenty metres; about 230 steps, free, and mobbed between 11:00 and 16:00 in summer.

places.name: The Writers' Resort
places.note: Two buildings on the same headland as the monastery: a 1932 constructivist block and Gevorg Kochar's 1963 glass lounge on stilts. Still in use, still mostly ignored, and the best modernism in Armenia.

places.name: Hayravank
places.note: Ninth century, small, right on the water on the west shore, with a khachkar field around it; ten minutes off the highway and you will likely have it to yourself.

places.name: The khachkar field at Noratus
places.note: Close to a thousand carved cross-stones from the tenth to the seventeenth century standing in a working village cemetery, with cows in among them; the Jugha field that was bigger was bulldozed, so this is what is left.

places.name: Tsaghkunk Restaurant and Glkhatun
places.note: A village restaurant project ten minutes off the lake doing old Gegharkunik recipes properly, with lavash out of the tonir next door; book, because it fills with Yerevan weekenders.

places.name: Grilled ishkhan at a lakeside shack
places.note: Sevan trout on a charcoal grill with lavash and a beer, eaten at a plastic table; the wild ishkhan is protected so what you get is farmed, and the shacks north of Sevan town are better than the ones in it.

places.name: Swimming at Tsapatagh
places.note: The east shore is quieter, cleaner and an hour further round than the resort strip; the water is 1,900m up and tops out near 20C in August, which is colder than it sounds.

places.name: The Artanish peninsula
places.note: A dry grass headland on the north east corner with no facilities and the best wide view of the lake; a rough track in, and worth it only if you have your own car and half a day.

places.name: Vanevan
places.note: A 903 monastery on the far south east shore that sees almost no visitors; only makes sense if you are driving the full circuit of the lake rather than doubling back.

places.name: The fish and crayfish stalls on the Sevan road
places.note: Smoked sig, dried crayfish and whitefish sold from tables on the shoulder of the M4; buy the smoked fish, and be aware the crayfish stocks here are in trouble.

places.name: Haghartsin
places.note: Tenth to thirteenth century, in beech forest 18km up a side valley, restored in 2013 on money from the ruler of Sharjah; the refectory is the best room and the new stonework is obvious.

places.name: Goshavank
places.note: Twelfth century, named for the lawyer who wrote the first Armenian law code here, and holding Poghos's 1291 khachkar, which is the finest carved stone in the country.

places.name: Gosh Lake
places.note: An hour up through forest from Goshavank to a small green lake; muddy after rain, unremarkable at the top, and the walk itself is the reason to do it.

places.name: Parz Lake
places.note: Coach parties, pedalos, a zipline and a restaurant round a pond the size of a car park; every itinerary includes it and the Jukhtak walk is better in every way.

places.name: Sharambeyan Street
places.note: One restored block of nineteenth century wooden balconies with a woodcarver, a ceramicist and a couple of shops; it is small and it knows it, but the craftsmen are real.

places.name: The Jukhtak Vank and Matosavank loop
places.note: About 8km on marked Transcaucasian Trail from the west end of town to two small eleventh century monasteries in deep beech forest; leeches after heavy rain, otherwise the best half day here.

places.name: The Dilijan mineral water fountain
places.note: The town made its name on this water and there is a public tap on the main road; it tastes of iron and salt and everyone fills bottles from it.

places.name: Kchuch
places.note: Everything comes out of a clay pot, which is what kchuch means; the lamb and the mushroom pots are the ones to order and the terrace is the best seat in town.

places.name: Cafe #2
places.note: A small room doing soups, trout and khashlama without ceremony; the sort of place that is full of locals at 14:00 and empty at 19:00.

places.name: Haykanoush at the Old Dilijan complex
places.note: Tufenkian's restaurant on the restored street, doing Tavush village cooking with a decent Armenian list; more polished and pricier than Kchuch, and fine for a last night.

places.name: Lastiver and the Yenokavan zipline
places.note: Forty minutes north of Dilijan: a cable line over the Khachaghbyur gorge, then a steep walk down to caves and a waterfall on the Lastiver river; wet, slippery, and the one genuinely adventurous thing in the north.

places.name: Khor Virap
places.note: The pit where Gregory the Illuminator was held for thirteen years, on a hill on the Turkish border with Ararat directly behind it; the church is ordinary and the view is the entire point, so go at dawn before the haze.

places.name: Noravank
places.note: Momik's 1339 two-storey Astvatsatsin with the cantilevered outside stairs, in a red limestone canyon 8km off the highway; late afternoon turns the cliffs the same colour as the building.

places.name: Areni-1 cave
places.note: The 4100 BC wine press and vats that make the six thousand year claim real, plus the world's oldest leather shoe, which is in the Yerevan museum not here; it is a dim hole with good signage and takes forty minutes.

places.name: Old Bridge Winery
places.note: A family cellar where Musho pours Areni Noir and a pomegranate wine in his own yard; call ahead, expect no tasting room polish, and expect to be fed.

places.name: Trinity Canyon Vineyards
places.note: The serious end of Vayots Dzor: Areni Noir reserve, Voskeat and a few skin contact whites, tasted on a terrace over the Arpa gorge. Open daily April to October, by appointment the rest of the year.

places.name: Hin Areni
places.note: The largest of the quality Areni producers and the easiest to walk into without booking; five wines for about 4,000 dram and a straightforward cellar tour.

places.name: Momik Wine Cube
places.note: A small producer with a tasting room built as a cube on the roadside; the natural-leaning Areni and the khndoghni from Artsakh vines are worth asking for specifically.

places.name: Surb Astvatsatsin at Areni
places.note: Momik's 1321 church on the hill above the village, the trial run for what he then built at Noravank; free, empty, and a five minute drive up from the wineries.

places.name: The Selim caravanserai
places.note: A 1332 Orbelian caravanserai at 2,410m on the old road over to Lake Sevan, dark inside and intact; the pass road is closed by snow from roughly November to April.

places.name: Smbataberd
places.note: A ridge fortress above the Yeghegis valley reached by an hour of steep walking from Artabuynk; walls, wind, no shade, and nobody else up there.

places.name: Areni Wine Factory
places.note: The big roadside operation every bus stops at, pouring semi-sweet pomegranate wine into plastic cups; the small cellars a kilometre away are making the wine you came for.

places.name: Jermuk
places.note: Mineral water town with a 70m waterfall and a Soviet drinking gallery, 50km and an hour each way off the M2; on an eight day trip that hour costs you the wineries, so leave it.

places.name: Old Khndzoresk and the swinging bridge
places.note: An abandoned cave village down both sides of a gorge, crossed by a 160m suspension bridge built by villagers in 2012; free, a steep set of stairs each way, and much better than the photographs suggest.

places.name: The Old Goris cave district
places.note: Rock cones and cut cave rooms on the slope above town, reached on foot from the centre in twenty minutes; no ticket, no signs, and no one there.

places.name: Zorats Karer
places.note: 223 standing basalt stones at 1,770m, many bored through with holes. The world's oldest observatory claim comes from a radiophysicist and archaeologists reject it; it reads as a Bronze Age necropolis and it is still a good hour on a windy plateau.

places.name: The Goris grid on foot
places.note: A Russian imperial street plan from the 1870s of low stone houses with wooden balconies, laid out under cliffs; twenty minutes end to end and the most pleasant town to walk in the south.

places.name: Aksel Bakunts House-Museum
places.note: The house of the writer the Soviets shot in 1937, kept as it was, with a garden; small, in Armenian and Russian mostly, and the caretaker will talk if you let her.

places.name: Hin Khot
places.note: An abandoned village in the Vorotan gorge that needs 4km of walking each way on a poor path; twelfth century church, roofless houses, and no facilities of any kind.

places.name: Dinner at Mirhav
places.note: The stone hotel on the edge of the centre does the most reliable dinner in Goris: zhingyalov hats, trout, lamb, and Vayots Dzor wine by the glass. Book if you arrive after 20:00.

places.name: Tuti oghi at a Goris guesthouse
places.note: Home distilled mulberry spirit, poured from an unlabelled bottle, usually about 55 percent. Syunik's real drink and every guesthouse has a cousin who makes it.

places.name: Tour Baza and the Goris draught beer
places.note: A Soviet tourist base above the town, still open, with the local Goris beer on tap and the whole grid laid out below; scruffy and the view does the work.

places.name: The Goris market
places.note: Small, mostly greens, cheese and honey from the surrounding villages; the place to pick up zhingyalov hats greens and mulberry syrup before the drive to Tatev.

places.name: The Vorotan pass viewpoint
places.note: 2,344m on the highway with the whole Vorotan gorge system opening below and the road switchbacking down into Goris; a pull-off, a monument and ten minutes.

places.name: The Wings of Tatev cableway
places.note: 5.7km and about twelve minutes each way, up to 320m above the Vorotan gorge, and it is the longest reversible cable car in the world. Closed every Monday, and it stops in winds over 50kph.

places.name: Tatev Monastery
places.note: Ninth century, on a basalt promontory over a 500m gorge, and the seat of a medieval university that taught here until 1435; free, and quiet again by 16:00 once the cable car crowd has gone back.

places.name: The Tatev oil mill
places.note: A restored medieval press inside the monastery walls with the wooden beam and stone vats back in working order; twenty minutes and the best explanation on the site of how the monastery actually fed itself.

places.name: Satan's Bridge
places.note: A natural travertine arch over the Vorotan with warm mineral springs and yellow and orange mineral crust in the caves under it; the water is about 25C, the changing arrangements are nonexistent, and the car park is a mess.

places.name: Tatevi Anapat
places.note: A seventeenth century hermitage on the gorge floor below the monastery, reached by a steep walk down the old road; ruined, roofless, unvisited, and about ninety minutes back up.

places.name: Shaki waterfall
places.note: An 18m fall on the Shaki river, forty minutes from Halidzor and easy to combine with Zorats Karer; the flow is diverted to a small hydro plant, so it can be reduced to a trickle outside spring.

places.name: The gorge lookout at Halidzor station
places.note: The terrace beside the lower cable car station, looking straight down the Vorotan; worth the ten minutes while you wait for a cabin, and free whether or not you ride.

places.name: Lunch at a Tatev village house
places.note: Two or three families in the village cook for visitors with a couple of hours notice: khashlama, village cheese, herbs, bread. The cafe at the lower station is the alternative and it is worse.

places.name: The old road down from Tatev
places.note: Ride up, then walk the switchbacks down to Satan's Bridge and have the car meet you: about 8km, 600m of descent, no shade and no water on the way.

places.name: The Harsnadzor watchtower
places.note: A restored medieval signal tower on the gorge rim on the driving route to Tatev, with barrel cabins beside it; a stop rather than a destination, and the view is the same one the cable car gives you for free.

outings.why: The whole central ring is walkable: the square and the History Museum, up Abovyan to the Matenadaran, across to the Cascade, down to Saryan for wine. Flat, shadeless in July and August, and the museums shut by 18:00.
outings.name: Yerevan on foot: Republic Square, the Cascade and Saryan Street
outings.season: All year. April to June and September to October are the san
outings.fallback: Matenadaran, the Parajanov Museum and a long lunch if it rains.

outings.why: Forty five minutes out to the temple, down into the gorge for the basalt columns, then up the valley to the cave church at Geghard, with lavash baking and khorovats in Garni in between. Both sites are mobbed between 11:00 and 14:00, so run
outings.name: Garni and Geghard
outings.season: All year. The Symphony of Stones track is bad after snow or
outings.fallback: Geghard alone plus lunch in Garni, skipping the gorge track.

outings.why: The seat of the Armenian Church 20km west, plus the ruined 7th century round cathedral on the way back. Half a day, entirely flat, and best combined with the airport run at either end of the trip.
outings.name: Echmiadzin and Zvartnots
outings.fallback: Echmiadzin Treasury only, 90 minutes door to door by marshrutka.

outings.why: The peninsula churches and the Writers' Resort, then 40 minutes down the west shore to the khachkar field at Noratus and lunch at Tsaghkunk. Done as the drive between Yerevan and Dilijan it costs you nothing extra; done as a return trip fro
outings.name: Sevanavank and Noratus
outings.season: May to October. The lake is bleak and windy from November to
outings.fallback: Sevanavank and a trout lunch only, three hours.

outings.why: Two monasteries in beech forest on opposite sides of Dilijan with an hour of uphill walking between Goshavank and the lake. Short drives, no altitude problem, and the forest holds mist most mornings until about 10:00.
outings.name: Haghartsin, Goshavank and the Gosh lake walk
outings.season: May to October for the walk. The monasteries are reachable a
outings.fallback: The two monasteries by car, three hours, no walking.

outings.why: Eight kilometres of marked Transcaucasian Trail from the west edge of town to two eleventh century ruins in dense forest and back. Gentle, well signed, and genuinely empty. Leeches after heavy rain.
outings.name: The Jukhtak Vank and Matosavank loop
outings.fallback: Sharambeyan Street and the Dilijan mineral spring, an hour.

outings.why: Forty minutes south to the monastery on the Turkish border with Ararat filling the sky behind it. The mountain is only visible early, and on a hazy afternoon there is nothing here worth the drive.
outings.name: Khor Virap and the Ararat plain
outings.season: All year. Best in the hour after sunrise, and clearest from
outings.fallback: Roll it into the drive south to Areni instead of making a separate trip.

outings.why: The cave with the 4100 BC wine press, two working cellars doing Areni Noir and Voskeat properly, and Noravank in the red canyon at the end of the afternoon. The catch is the driving: either sleep in Areni or hire a driver, because tasting f
outings.name: The Areni wine road: Noravank, Areni-1 and two cellars
outings.season: All year for the monastery, April to October for walk-in tas
outings.fallback: Noravank and one cellar, four hours.

outings.why: The 1332 caravanserai at 2,410m on the old Silk Road crossing, then back down into the Yeghegis valley and an hour of steep walking up to a ridge fortress. The pass road shuts under snow, usually November to April.
outings.name: Selim pass and Smbataberd
outings.fallback: The Yeghegis valley churches and the Jewish cemetery at Yeghegis, three hours, no climbing.

outings.why: Forty minutes from Goris to the Halidzor station, twelve minutes across the gorge, three hours on the promontory including the oil mill, then Satan's Bridge on the drive back. It is shut every Monday and it stops in high wind, so build a sp
outings.name: The Tatev cableway and monastery
outings.season: All year, except Mondays and the late November maintenance w
outings.fallback: Drive to Tatev on the road through Halidzor and Shinuhayr, about 90 minutes each way, and skip the cable car.

outings.why: Fifteen minutes out of Goris, then a long stair descent into a gorge full of abandoned cave houses and a 160m suspension bridge across it. Free, steeper than it looks coming back up, and good in the last two hours of light.
outings.name: Old Khndzoresk and the swinging bridge
outings.season: All year. Icy steps in winter.
outings.fallback: The Old Goris cave district on foot from the town centre, 90 minutes.

outings.why: An hour west along the M2 over the 2,344m pass to the standing stones above Sisian, with Shaki waterfall ten minutes further on. Windy and exposed, and best done as a stop on the drive north rather than a return trip.
outings.name: Zorats Karer and the Vorotan pass
outings.season: May to October. The pass gets snow and fog from November.
outings.fallback: Shaki waterfall only, on the way past.

destination.name: Armenia: Yerevan, Dilijan and the south
destination.pitch: A small, poor, extremely old country where the food and the wine are the surprise and the monasteries are the reason you booked, best done as four bases on one road that runs north to Dilijan and south to Tatev.
destination.caveat: The borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan are closed, so everything moves on two roads out of Yerevan and the drive to Tatev is four hours each way on a highway that carries Iranian trucks; add the 2020 and 2023 wars in Nagorno-Karabakh, which ended with a hundred thousand refugees arriving in exactly  Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Yerevan is pink tufa, Soviet planning and a young crowd that eats late; it is compact, cheap and good for three nights, and it is not why you came.
because.food: Six thousand years of winemaking that only restarted commercially in the 2000s, a capital with real cooking on Saryan and Tumanyan, brandy that Churchill drank, and lavash out of a clay pit in any village that will have you.
because.nature: Beech forest and marked trail around Dilijan, a 500m basalt gorge at Tatev, and a lake at 1,900m, but the scale is modest and the Caucasus proper is over the border in Georgia.
because.culture: The first state to adopt Christianity, seventeen thousand manuscripts in one building, carved cross-stones nobody else makes, and a genocide memorial that reframes everything you see afterwards.
because.adventure: The Transcaucasian Trail through Dilijan, the zipline and caves at Lastiver, and the walk down the old road from Tatev to the gorge floor.
because.relaxation: Low. Long lunches and a guesthouse terrace in Areni are as restful as it gets, and the driving days are long.
because.exploration: Half the good things here have no ticket office, no fence and nobody at them: Havuts Tar, Tatevi Anapat, Hin Khot, the Old Goris caves.
